e.etymology: A spelling of Todd, from a surname based on the Middle English and northern dialect word tod, fox.
namesakes: Tod (the fox in Disney's The Fox and the Hound)
e.note: Tod is the German word for death.

assoc.t: Tod, the fox in Disney's The Fox and the Hound

e.etymology: A spelling of Lindsay, a Scottish surname taken from Lindsey in Lincolnshire, Old English for the isle of Lind, the old name of Lincoln.
An old Irish name from donn, a word meaning both brown and chief or noble; Donn is the lord of the dead in Irish myth. Americans have mostly used it as a spelling of Don, short for Donald.
A spelling of Teresa, a Spanish name of uncertain origin, perhaps from Greek therizein, to harvest. Saint Teresa of Ávila carried it across Europe.
A pet form of Nicole and Nicola, and for boys of Nicholas, all from Greek Nikolaos, joining nike, victory, and laos, people.
A German and Danish short form of Margareta, from Greek margarites, pearl. German and Scandinavian immigrants brought it to America in the 1800s.

assoc.t: Meta, parent company of Facebook and Instagram

e.note: Since 2021 Meta has been the name of Facebook's parent company, and meta is a common word for self-referential.

e.etymology: From an English surname joining Old English gar, spear, and feld, field. Use as a first name surged in 1881, the year President James A. Garfield was assassinated.

assoc.t: Garfield, the lasagna-loving comic strip cat

e.note: Garfield the orange comic strip cat owns this name for most Americans.

e.etymology: From a Norman surname and French place name, Old French grant, large, plus ville, settlement. The baronial family's name came from Grainville in Normandy, Guarin's town.
Usually explained as a pet form of Tressa, itself a short form of Theresa.
A phonetic spelling of Jacqueline, the French feminine of Jacques, which is the French form of Jacob and James.
A 1990s spelling that sits between Tierra, Spanish for earth or land, and Tiara, the jeweled crown.
The French form of a Germanic name joining berht, bright, and hramn, raven; the ending was later also read as rand, shield rim. Its English cousin is Bertram.
The Irish form of Donald, from Gaelic Domhnall, an old Celtic name meaning world ruler. In America it has also been a pared-down spelling of Donald.
From the Italian and Latin word palma, palm. As an Italian given name it is traditionally tied to Palm Sunday.
A spelling of Drusilla, the feminine pet form of the Roman family nickname Drusus. A Drusilla appears in the Acts of the Apostles.
George with the feminine ending -etta, a twin of French Georgette. George comes from Greek georgos, farmer or earth-worker.
A phonetic spelling of Frieda, a German name from Friede, peace, also a short form of names such as Friederike.
A form of Shadrach, the name given to one of the three young men thrown into the fiery furnace in the Book of Daniel. Shedrick also exists as a surname.
A spelling of Chrissy, the pet form of Christine and Christina, from Latin Christianus, a follower of Christ.
In American use a spelling of Corey or Cory. As a surname Corry is a short form of Irish McCorry or a variant of Scottish Corrie.
The English word fairy used as a name, mostly in the American South around 1900. The word came from Old French faerie, the land of the fays.
e.note: An ordinary word, and also a dated slur for a gay man.

assoc.t: fairy, the tiny winged being of folklore
fairy, a dated slur for a gay man

e.etymology: A North German and Frisian short form of Johannes, or John, from Hebrew Yochanan, God is gracious. In America it has also been a spelling of Jan.
namesakes: Jann Wenner (co-founder of Rolling Stone magazine)

e.etymology: A feminine pet form of Charles made with the ending -ie, used mostly in the American South. Charles goes back to a Germanic word for a free man.
An American name that rose in 1977, the year LeVar Burton, born Levardis, starred as Kunta Kinte in the miniseries Roots.
namesakes: LeVar Burton (Reading Rainbow host and Star Trek actor)

assoc.t: LeVar Burton of Reading Rainbow and Star Trek

e.etymology: As a first name, a spelling of Ricki or Rikki. Ricci is also a common Italian surname, from a nickname for someone with curly hair, said REE-chee.
From a surname that is a variant of Terry, and also a spelling of the first names Torrey and Tory.
A feminine form of Kyle made with the ending -ene. Kyle is a Scottish surname and place name from Gaelic caol, a narrow strait.
A pet form of Greek Aristotelis, or Aristotle. American use peaked in 1974, when Telly Savalas was starring in Kojak.
e.note: Telly is British slang for television.

e.etymology: A pet form of Emmanuel, from Hebrew Immanuel, God is with us, and of the Spanish form Manuel.

assoc.t: collie, the herding dog breed of Lassie

e.note: Collie is the name of a dog breed, the first thing most people will think of.
